meta.description: TikTok's app caps uploads at about 72 MB on Android and 288 MB on iOS; uploading from tiktok.com allows around 10 GB and up to 60 minutes. See what fits, then compress or trim your video in your browser — nothing uploaded.
og.title: TikTok video size limit: 72 MB Android · 288 MB iOS · 10 GB web
og.description: The three TikTok limits, why the web upload is the way round them, and how to fit a video in your browser.
hero.title: TikTok video size limit
hero.lead: TikTok has three very different limits depending on where you upload from: about 72 MB in the Android app, about 288 MB in the iOS app, and around 10 GB from tiktok.com in a browser. Videos can be up to 60 minutes long, though that ceiling is still rolling out account by account. If the app rejects a video, uploading the same file from the website usually works.
qa.h2: TikTok upload limits at a glance
qa.r3.k: The easy way round the app limits
qa.r3.v: Upload from tiktok.com in a browser: the same account, a far higher size limit, and no need to compress at all.
qa.after: None of these figures is officially published — they are the practical limits users hit, checked against TikTok's help pages and current builds. The Android figure is the one that bites: a minute of good-quality phone footage is often already over 72 MB.
tool.h2: Fit your video under the app limit
tool.lead: Drop the video below and pick a target — 50 MB clears the Android app's cap with room to spare, and the compressor spends the budget where it shows least. It runs on your own device, so nothing is uploaded until you post. Need to shorten the clip instead? The trimmer cuts to the exact second.
fit.h2: How much video fits in 50 MB?
fit.lead: Length decides the picture size: the same 50 MB is spread across every second. These rows are what this compressor actually produces from a typical phone recording — full HD, 30 frames a second, with sound — at a 50 MB target.
fit.caption: What 50 MB gives you at different video lengths
fit.r1.q: Full HD at the original quality — nothing is lost
fit.r2.q: About half of full HD each way — clear on any phone
fit.r3.q: Reduced size — fine on a phone, soft on a laptop
fit.r4.q: Small picture; watchable, blocky on a big screen
fit.after: TikTok recompresses every upload to its own settings, so there is no point compressing below what the app requires — pick the largest target that fits, keep the picture as good as it can be, and let TikTok do the rest.
over.h2: App says the video is too large? Two fixes
over.p1: First, try the website. Log in at tiktok.com, use the upload button, and the same video that the Android app refused will go through — the web limit is roughly a hundred times higher. Second, if you must post from the phone, compress to under the app's limit here; at 50 MB a minute of full-HD footage stays sharp.
over.p2: Everything on this page runs locally in your browser — your video never leaves your device, and there is no account or watermark. Not sure a clip will fit at a decent quality? The bitrate calculator tells you the picture size a target supports for your video's exact length.
faq.q1: Why does TikTok say my video is too large?
faq.a1: Most likely you're uploading from the Android app, which caps files at about 72 MB — a minute of good phone footage can exceed that. The iOS app allows about 288 MB, and tiktok.com in a browser around 10 GB. Upload from the website, or compress the video first.
faq.q2: How long can a TikTok video be?
faq.a2: Up to 60 minutes, though the 60-minute option is still being rolled out account by account; many accounts see 10 minutes as their ceiling. Length applies whether you upload from the app or the web.
faq.q3: Does TikTok reduce video quality on upload?
faq.a3: Yes — every upload is recompressed to TikTok's own settings. That's why compressing below the app's limit is pointless: aim for the largest file the upload route allows and keep the source as sharp as possible.
faq.q4: Is the web upload limit really 10 GB?
faq.a4: About that — it isn't published, but files of several gigabytes upload from tiktok.com without complaint. Length, not size, is what stops a web upload.
faq.q5: Is my video uploaded when I compress it here?
faq.a5: No. Compression runs in your browser on your own device — there is no server, no account and no watermark. The only place your video goes is where you post or send it yourself.
